label: Strongly improving
rationale: Cost to LEO has fallen ~40× from the Space Shuttle era ($54,500/kg) to $1,500/kg for Falcon Heavy. With Starship operational, another 10–100× reduction is possible by 2030.

label: Distant — currently at 3.1%
rationale: Annual mass to orbit reached a record 3,141 tonnes in 2025, ~3% of the 100,000-tonne threshold. Reaching it requires ~1,000 Starship-class flights per year; at current ~20–40% growth it would take 15–20 years, with the earliest plausible date in the early 2030s.

label: Distant — targeting mid-2030s
rationale: No crewed lunar landing has occurred since 1972; Starship HLS delays push the first Artemis crewed landing to ~2028, and a permanent base is realistic only by the mid-2030s. ISRU remains unproven on planetary surfaces, as VIPER's cancellation and revival illustrate.

label: Approaching — first products expected 2026–2027
rationale: No space-manufactured product is on retail shelves yet, but demonstrations are accelerating: Varda has completed five manufacturing missions with successful reentries, and ZBLAN fiber, bioprinting and semiconductor payloads progressed. First FDA clinical trial using space-manufactured compounds is projected for 2026–2027 and first commercial drug sale for the late 2020s.

label: Progressing: 3,194 t to orbit in 2025 (3.2% of 100 kt/yr); +45%/yr 5-yr trend, ETA ~2034
rationale: Annual payload mass to orbit, the milestone's own quantity, rose from 797 t (2021) to 3,194 t (2025). Its log-linear trend over that 5-year window is +44.7%/yr, against +11.3%/yr for the previous non-overlapping window (2016-2020), so the growth is clear and accelerating. Extrapolating the current window trend reaches 100,000 t/yr about 9.3 years after 2025 (around 2034), inside the 5-10 year band. Sustaining that pace depends on Starship reaching operational cadence, which is not demonstrated (three 2025 test-flight losses, two successes; ~85% of mass is SpaceX), so the ETA is not ≤5 years and not green; the slower 2025 step (+21.6%) is a single observation and does not flip the status.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity (annual payload mass to orbit) with a credible trend-extrapolated ETA of 5-10 years; not green because no demonstrated precursor at relevant scale (operational Starship cadence) exists
basis.eta: ~2034 (100,000 t/yr reached ~9.3 yr after data year 2025 on the 2021-2025 log-linear trend; 2020-2025 endpoint CAGR 41.1%/yr gives ~2035)
basis.path: Trend extrapolation of payload-mass-to-orbit (JSR msatannual). Growth is driven by SpaceX (Falcon 9/Starlink, ~85% of 2025 mass); sustaining ~45%/yr past the late 2020s requires fully reusable Starship-class launch at high cadence
blockers: Technical: Starship not yet operational (2025: flights 7-9 lost ship or booster, flights 10-11 succeeded; no operational payload flights)
Concentration: ~85% of mass from one provider

window.sensitivity: 2016-2025 log-linear +30.0%/yr -> ETA ~13 yr after 2025 (~2038); 2024->2025 step +21.6% (adjacent points, not scored) -> ~17.6 yr
window.source: uv run ledger.py series rockets payload-mass-to-orbit --as-of 2026-09-30 (2021-2025 collector rows, 2020 legacy)

label: Progressing: no space-made product sold on Earth yet; repeated return demos, ETA 5-10 yrs
rationale: No event shows a space-manufactured product sold commercially on Earth, so the milestone is not achieved. There is measurable progress on the manufacturing half of the milestone: Varda reports five pharmaceutical-crystal missions with five successful reentries (W-1 in 2024 to W-5 in November 2025), Flawless Photonics has drawn more than 12 km of ZBLAN fiber on the ISS, and Space Forge has returned a semiconductor payload. The nearest route (Varda) names clinical trials as its next step, which implies a sale 5-10 years out. Any faster ETA rests only on proponent claims or market forecasts, which cannot lift the status, and it is not green because none of these precursors runs at commercial scale, and none has non-proponent corroboration.

label: Distant: no crewed landing since 1972, ISRU at gram-per-hour demos; ETA >10 yrs
rationale: No crew has landed on the Moon since 1972. The first Artemis crewed landing has slipped to 2028 or later, pending Starship HLS refuelling demonstrations, and NASA reopened the lander contract to rivals. Local-resource use has only reached demonstrations: MOXIE made up to 12 g/h of oxygen on Mars, molten regolith electrolysis has produced oxygen from simulant, and PRIME-1 sampled no ice.; food on the ISS is still 100% resupplied. A permanent base running 1+ year on local resources therefore has no evidenced path under 10 years; the mid-2030s dates (China ILRS 2035, Artemis base plans) are roadmaps and cannot shorten the ETA.

basis.rule: Milestone red: ETA over 10 years on every evidenced path; the precursors (crewed surface access, ISRU and closed-loop life support at base scale) are not demonstrated, and the shorter dates are roadmaps only

label: Progressing: 3,194 t to orbit in 2025 (3.2% of 100 kt/yr); +45%/yr 5-yr trend, ETA ~2035
rationale: Annual payload mass to orbit, the milestone's own quantity, rose from 797 t (2021) to 3,194 t (2025), a +44.7%/yr log-linear trend (doubling every 1.9 yr) against +11.3%/yr in 2016-2020. That trend closes the 31x gap in 9.3 years (2034). The growth rides on a single Falcon 9 fleet (~165 launches, ~85% of mass), so reaching ~1,000 flights/yr of a 100 t vehicle means handing the trend over to Starship; relay scenarios give 2034-2039. The median is 2035 (80% range 2032-2044): yellow, not green, because the median is more than 5 years away and no operational Starship flight exists.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity with median ETA <= made_at + 10 yr (p50 2035); not green (p50 > 5 yr, no precursor at relevant scale)

eta.method: trend (log-linear on payload-mass-to-orbit) combined with a vehicle-relay scenario model (Falcon 9 saturating -> Starship ramp) and a reference-class check
eta.calc: gap 100000/3194 = 31.3x (4.97 doublings). Log-linear fits (series rockets payload-mass-to-orbit --as-of 2026-10-06): 2021-25 +44.7%/yr -> ln(31.3)/0.370 = 9.3 yr -> 2034.3 (80% CI of slope 2033.4-2035.5); 2020-25 +43.0% -> 2034.6; 2016-25 +30.0% -> 2038.1; 2024->25 step +21.6% (single step, not trend) -> 2042.6. Relay: legacy fleet +20%/yr capped at 8 kt + Starship from 10 flights in 2027 at 100 t/flight: flights x2/yr -> 2033.5, +80% -> 2034.7, +60% -> 2036.6, +45% (Falcon 9 analog 26->165 flights 2020-25) -> 2039.2; start 2029 at 5 flights +45% -> 2043.0. p10: +60%/yr sustained -> 2032.3. p90: +20%/yr -> 2043.9. p50 weights the 2021-25 trend and central relay cases -> 2035. Prev v1 ETA ~2034.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: operational Starship payload flights (Starlink V3) at >= monthly cadence in 2026-27, ship reuse, a 2026 JSR total >= ~4,600 t (+45%). Later: a 2026 total <= ~3,800 t (Falcon 9 saturation with no hand-off), more Starship losses, no second reusable heavy provider ramping.

basis.path: Own quantity, JSR annual payload mass to orbit. Near term: Falcon 9/Starlink (~85% of mass) plus constellations (Guowang) and new reusable boosters (New Glenn). 100 kt/yr needs ~1,000 flights/yr of a ~100 t fully reusable vehicle (Starship class).
blockers: Technical: Starship not operational (2025: flights 7-9 failures, 10-11 successes; no operational payload flight)
Concentration: ~85% of 2025 mass from one provider; Falcon 9 cadence growth slowing (2024->25 +21.6%)

label: Progressing: no space-made product sold yet; Varda 5 returns, ZBLAN 12 km, ETA ~2031
rationale: No event shows a space-manufactured product sold commercially on Earth. In-space production with return is repeated, though: Varda has flown five pharmaceutical-crystal missions with five reentries and names clinical trials as its next step, Flawless Photonics has drawn more than 12 km of ZBLAN fiber with quality verification ongoing, and Space Forge has returned a semiconductor payload. A competing-paths model (Varda trials plus a ~3.5-yr regulatory floor; low annual hazards for a ZBLAN or other materials sale) gives a median of 2031 (80% range 2028-2039). It is yellow, not green: every precursor is gram-scale, and the evidence comes from the proponents themselves.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: median ETA <= 5 yr (p50 2031) but the path lacks green's conditions (no precursor at commercial scale, no non-proponent corroboration) -> yellow per RUBRIC.md §4

eta.method: structural floor (clinical/regulatory programme) plus annual hazard per path, combined by competing-paths Monte Carlo; cross-checked against a reference class and discounted proponent dates
eta.calc: Gap: 0 -> 1 commercial sale. Path A (Varda pharma): trial start now+lognormal(median 1.0 yr) + programme lognormal(median 3.5 yr, sigma 0.35), P(fail) 0.40 -> conditional 2029.9/2031.4/2033.5. Path B (ZBLAN fiber): 6%/yr hazard from 2027. Path C (other materials): 3%/yr rising to 8%/yr as launch supply grows (payload-mass-to-orbit +44.7%/yr 2021-25). Earliest of A/B/C (N=200k): p10 2028.1, p50 2031.1, p90 2038.6; P(by Oct 2031) 0.61, P(by Oct 2036) 0.87. Reference class: drug reformulation from proof of concept to market takes ~5-8 yr; first Varda return in 2024 -> 2029-32. Proponent 'first drug sale late 2020s' x1.5 -> ~2031. Prev v1 ETA was a band ('5-10 years').
eta.cruxes: Earlier: an IND or trial start with a space-made formulation; a positive ZBLAN quality result plus a supply contract; any paid offtake of a space-made material; verifying whether NBS SRM 1960 (Shuttle-made latex spheres sold from 1985; not in the ledger) already meets the wording. Later: Varda pivots to reentry services only; the ZBLAN verification fails; trials slip past 2028.

basis.path: Varda free-flying capsules (pharmaceutical crystals -> clinical trials -> approved drug sale); Flawless Photonics ZBLAN fiber (ISS) -> qualified fiber sale; Space Forge semiconductor materials; Redwire crystallization/biofabrication. Launch supply growth (Deluge series) lowers access cost.
blockers: Regulatory/technical: no product has passed qualification for sale (pharma needs trials and approval; ZBLAN quality verification ongoing)
Evidence: all supporting events are legacy and mostly proponent-sourced
Definitional: whether historical items (e.g. NBS SRM 1960 space-made microspheres) count as 'beyond novelty': gather request

label: Distant: no crewed Moon landing since 1972; ISRU at 12 g/h demos; Artemis III >=2028; ETA ~2039
rationale: A 1-year base on local resources needs this chain: a crewed landing, then a habitat with continuous occupancy, then ISRU at base scale, then a year of operation. No crew has landed since 1972, Artemis III has slipped to ~Sep 2028 or later, and China targets ~2030. ISRU is at demonstration scale (MOXIE 12 g/h of O2; no ice sampled). Modelling both programmes, with an ~8-year landing-to-base gap and a 1-year operating floor, gives a median of 2039 (p10 2036; p90 open, as either programme may stall), which is more than 10 years out, so red.

basis.rule: Milestone red: median ETA 2039 > made_at + 10 yr (RUBRIC.md §4: Distant)

eta.method: structural floor chain (crewed landing -> base -> 1 yr operation) with discounted proponent landing dates and a reference-class base gap, simulated by Monte Carlo over US and Chinese programmes
eta.calc: US: landing 2028.7 + lognormal slip (median 1.5 yr), P(abandon) 0.35. China: landing 2030 + lognormal slip (median 1.0 yr), P(abandon) 0.30. Landing-to-base gap lognormal(median 8 yr, 80% 4.8-13.3; reference class: Tiangong first module -> continuous crew ~1 yr, but 19 yr from China's first crewed flight; ISS 2 yr from first module, 16 yr from Freedom start) + 1 yr operating floor. Conditional ETAs: US 2036.0/2039.6/2045.4, China 2036.9/2040.3/2045.8; earliest of the two (N=200k): p10 2036.1, p50 2039.4, P(neither) 0.105 -> p90 open. Cross-checks: ILRS basic base 2035 x1.5 -> ~2040; Artemis III slip 2024 -> >=2028 (factor ~2.25). ISRU sizing: 4 crew x 0.84 kg O2/day = ~140 g/h, ~12x MOXIE's 12 g/h, so ISRU is not the binding gap. Driver: lift capacity (payload-mass-to-orbit 3,194 t in 2025, +44.7%/yr; Deluge p50 2035). Prev v1 ETA was '>10 years', a band.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: an orbital propellant-transfer demo in 2026-27; a crewed landing (Artemis III or China) on schedule; a funded surface habitat; VIPER finding accessible ice. Later: Artemis III slips past 2029; SLS/Gateway cancelled without replacement; ILRS crewed phase re-dated after 2040.

basis.path: Artemis (Starship or rival HLS, south-pole presence) and China's ILRS (crewed landing ~2030, basic base 2035, both projections). ISRU precursors: MOXIE O2, MRE O2 from simulant, VIPER ice prospecting (late 2027). Life-support precursors: Tiangong 100% O2 regeneration, ISS 98% water recovery, Lunar Palace 1 80% food for 105 days.
blockers: Technical: no crewed lander demonstrated; HLS needs orbital refuelling (10-12 Starship flights)
Technical: ISRU at gram-per-hour demo scale; no ice sampled in situ
Technical: food still 100% resupplied on ISS
Programmatic: HLS contract reopened to rivals; proposed FY2026 NASA cuts

eta.method: trend (log-linear on payload-mass-to-orbit, the current 5-yr rate as the median per §4.1 step 3) with a Starship hand-off check; slower long-run rate as p90; reference-class cross-check
eta.calc: gap 100000/3194.0 = 31.3x (4.97 doublings). Series (series rockets payload-mass-to-orbit --as-of 2026-10-12) 2021-25: 797.4, 1046.4, 1462.8, 2625.9, 3194.0 t -> slope 0.370 +/- 0.032 SE = +44.7%/yr; ln(31.3)/0.370 = 9.32 yr. Calendar-year totals: 3194 x 1.447^9 = 88.9 kt (2034, short), x 1.447^10 = 128.5 kt (2035) -> p50 2035 (same on the fitted line, fit2025 3,334 t). Hand-off: with the legacy fleet at +20%/yr capped at 6-8 kt, the trend needs ~8/21/140/830 Starship flights x 100 t in 2026/27/30/34 (+69%/yr from 2027). label: Progressing: 3,194 t to orbit in 2025 (3.2% of 100 kt/yr); +45%/yr 5-yr trend, ETA ~2035
rationale: Annual payload mass to orbit, the milestone's own quantity, rose from 797 t (2021) to 3,194 t (2025): +44.7%/yr log-linear (doubling every 1.9 yr) against +11.3%/yr in 2016-2020. At the measured rate the 2034 total is 88.8 kt and the 2035 total 128.5 kt, so the median first 100-kt year is 2035 (p10 2033). The 1968-2019 plateau shows a ramp can stall for decades, so the chance of reaching 100 kt/yr by 2100 is put at 0.88 and p90 is open. Yellow, not green: the median is over 5 years away and the Falcon 9 to Starship hand-off has no operational precursor in the ledger.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity and median ETA 2035 <= made_at + 10 yr (RUBRIC.md §4); not green because p50 > made_at + 5 yr and there is no demonstrated precursor at relevant scale (no operational Starship payload flight)

eta.method: trend (log-linear on payload-mass-to-orbit, current 5-yr rate as the median, §4.1 step 3) with a plateau-risk reference class for p_achieved; Monte Carlo over the growth rate; long-run rate on the late side

Measurement gap: no 2026 total yet (JSR reports after year-end) and no faster YTD-2026 tally in the ledger, so the extrapolation runs from 2025 and the gap is not read as a slowdown. p_achieved 0.88: the 1957-68 ramp (~+43%/yr) plateaued at ~300-1,400 t for ~50 yr; failure needs a near-flat century (+5%/yr from 2025 still reaches 100 kt by 2096). MC N=400k: log-slope split-normal median 0.370, sd 0.105 below / 0.078 above (80% +25% to +60%/yr), 12% never -> unconditional p10 2033, p50 2035 (conditional 0.57 quantile), p90 null; if achieved 2033/2035/2040. Prev v3: 2033/2035/2041, no p_achieved.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: JSR 2026 total >= ~4,600 t (on trend 4,622 t) or a partial-2026 tally above trend; operational Starship payload flights (Starlink V3) at >= monthly cadence in 2026-27; ship reuse. Later: 2026 total <= ~3,800 t (second sub-trend year after +21.6%); further Starship losses; no second reusable heavy launcher ramping.
